decision.title: Streaming fixes from the book: text value templates, streamed xsl:iterate and xsl:for-each-group, //x from elements, child-path indexes (packet fix-3)
decision.summary: Text value templates in xsl:text stream as paths, xsl:iterate and grouping xsl:for-each-group over a path of steps become a , and the descendant pass hoists child-path filters so they are indexed.

body.p: , after , , , , , , , , . Book-12 found four problems on the 82 MB trace archive (100,000 traces, 633,333 spans); the newest drafts decide each. Measured with the release CLI (peak resident set, wall seconds); QT4 whole with the release drivers, case by case, after each change: XT40 12,283 (98 wrong error), XQ40 46,158, XP40 32,815 before and after, no outcome differs.

item.p: xsl:text (wrong result): the analysis took xsl:text as grounded and motionless, so a text value template in it read a shallow window (<xsl:text>{count(trace)}</xsl:text> gave 0). XSLT Streaming 4.0, 12.6.40: xsl:text follows the general rules, its content absorbed (12.5). Two downward selections in it are now XTSE3430, and a text value template, in xsl:text or a text node, is a streamed path: {count(trace)} at /traces 318.8 MB -> 11.1 MB.

xsl:iterate (12.6.22, guaranteed-streamable with a striding select): it was a streamed path, every node grounded before fn:scan ran (586 MB). Decided (glossary ): an xsl:iterate whose select is a path of steps is a stream point; its closure runs on each node's full window as the node passes, the STREAM's fold holding the iteration state, new flag SXML_IR_STREAM_FOLDS_ITERATIONS (src/ir_internal.h: the body's value is the state, its second member the STREAM's value for the node, a non-zero control ends the STREAM and skips the rest of origin's content). The outputs are a content LET (), delivered as made. first-slow.xsl 586.0 MB 7.55 s -> 11.1 MB 6.58 s; an output per trace 193 MB -> 11.1 MB. After xsl:break no body runs, but the rest of the document is still parsed (not built): Streaming 4.0, 2.5 lets a processor stop reading, but the principal stream cannot know that nothing after the element is read (trailing comments and processing instructions go to the mode). Rejected: a separate IR kind for iterations (the fold of carries the state).

xsl:for-each-group (12.6.19): group-by outside xsl:fork, and any xsl:sort, are roaming and free-ranging (XTSE3430, already so). group-adjacent, group-starting-with and group-ending-with without xsl:sort over a path of steps are now the same kind of stream point: a step closure keeps the pending group's pairs in an array (persistent append, ) and asks the grouping row () whether the node starts a group, comparing it with the group's first pair (its last for group-ending-with); a complete group goes to a body closure. A group is held while it forms, never the population: adjacent groups by route 598.3 MB 8.50 s -> 11.1 MB 8.33 s, output identical.

count(//x) from /traces ran on a tree (352 MB): 12.9.21 rewrites root(.) of a non-document to head(ancestor-or-self::node()), which is no pattern step, so "//x" is no scanning expression there (12.8.9's note: it streams only where the focus is a document node). Now XTSE3430, the documented outcome; from match="/" it streams in 11 MB.

Child paths and the filter index (, , ): /spans/span[@parent = $span/@id] in a loop filtered each origin's children apart, a FILTER input made anew each turn, never indexed (21.9 s over 3,000 traces). The descendant pass also pulls the links after a child step out of the path's MAP when they go on from each node alone, include a FILTER and are read once, before the path's DOCUMENT_ORDER (same nodes, same order, XPath 4.0, 4.6.2); the input is then loop-independent, hoisted and indexed: 0.30 s. No parallel mechanism; run-bench outputs byte-identical, times within noise.

fn:parse-json number-parser: not in the newest F&O 4.0 draft (17.4.4 has liberal, duplicates, escape, fallback, null and number-format: double, decimal, adaptive, all implemented). An unknown option is rejected (1.7, option parameter conventions); nothing to do.

Left: stopping the parse after a break; xsl:for-each-group with xsl:sort in xsl:fork; xsl:iterate and xsl:for-each-group with a select that is not a plain path of steps, or a body with stream points of its own (full windows per node, bounded by the node).
